title: Rollback's database restore reaches a bound production destination: requested means applied, not requested means untouched
description: Split from task-da60dc4b by governor ruling 21:25Z on worker-deb4c7d8's measurement: `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts:86-88` refuses `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` ("no database restoration port is bound to the selected deployment environment") because `BackupPorts.restoreDatabase` (task-95e68a8d, DONE) only verifies a dump inside a temporary isolated database and has no bound production destination. So 'requested -> the restore is applied' is unsatisfiable today and 'not requested -> untouched' is vacuous. This row binds the destination and makes both arms real. task-da60dc4b keeps the refusal's code+layer assertion and the no-restore-call assertion.
definitionOfDone: A production restore destination is bound per deployment environment (the selected environment's database, resolved through the existing environment credential seam - never process.env, never a browser-supplied URL); an environment with no bound destination keeps refusing `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` with code AND layer.

`deployment.rollback` with `restore: true` applies the recorded backup (the one named by the kept deploy receipt / backupRef) to that destination and the rollback receipt says so; `restore` not requested records NO restore call on the port - both arms asserted from the port's recorded calls.
A restore that fails leaves the schema as it was and the receipt REFUSED with the failing step named (code + layer); no automatic retry, no partial apply.

LIVE ARM on a disposable PostgreSQL through the production composition: backup, mutate the schema, rollback with `restore: true`, assert the schema is back; every container, temp tree and child process released in `finally` on every exit path; no connection value, SQL or password in logs or evidence.
Fresh focused daemon tests + `pnpm typecheck` EXIT 0 with a planted control; named broader gates per lease rules; paths declared; physical .js bridges for any new runtime module.

DO NOT CHANGE `restoreDatabase(path)` — its verify-in-an-isolated-container meaning is depended on by `scheduled-backup.ts:62` and must keep behaving identically; the new operation sits BESIDE it. No automatic retry and no partial apply (DoD 3): one attempt, and a failure is a failure.

implementationPlan.description: THE BINDING — NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-restore.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge, with a NAME-MATCHED `rollback-restore.test.ts` in step 4 (an unmatched name makes runtime-entrypoint.test.ts class the module TEST tier and call the bridge `unexpected`). IT ANSWERS TWO QUESTIONS AND NOTHING ELSE. (1) WHICH DATABASE: call `resolveDeployMigrationContext` for the rollback's admitted environment — DO NOT write a second resolver, DO NOT read `process.env`, DO NOT accept a URL from the request payload (DoD 1, epic rail 3). Forward its refusal code AND layer UNCHANGED; an environment whose destination will not resolve is the case that must still refuse `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` with code and layer (DoD 1). (2) WHICH DUMP — SETTLED, DO NOT REINTERPRET: restore the CURRENT deploy's PRE-MIGRATION dump, i.e. the backup taken before the migration being undone, which is the schema state the kept receipt ran against. Resolve it by the durable join: read the CURRENT deploy receipt for the environment, take its `decisionId`, and `readMigrationReceipt(store, projectId, decisionId)` — a deterministic key lookup, never a filename, SHA, latest-timestamp or arbitrary-requestId match. Take `backupRef` from THAT receipt. THE KEPT RECEIPT'S OWN backupRef IS THE WRONG DUMP: it predates the kept deploy's own migration and would rewind one step too far, discarding schema the kept deploy applied. If a reading of the DoD seems to want it, STOP AND REPORT rather than switching. REFUSE, NEVER SUBSTITUTE: no current receipt, no migration receipt, a null `backupRef`, or a dump whose bytes do not match what the receipt recorded each refuse with a stable code and the layer that answered, leaving the database untouched. Mint refusal details from a FIXED table keyed by code, the way `DEPLOY_MIGRATION_CONTEXT_DETAILS` does — no template, no interpolation, so no detail can be built out of a value just read. Keep the module under 250 lines.

WHICH DUMP — the CURRENT deploy's PRE-MIGRATION dump, implemented exactly as settled and NOT reinterpreted. `readCurrentDeployReceipt(store, projectId, environment)` -> `current.decisionId` -> `readMigrationReceipt(store, projectId, current.decisionId)` -> `backupRef`. Deterministic key lookup via the durable join (`deploy-command.ts:267` `requestId: decisionId`); no filename scan, no SHA search, no newest-timestamp match, no arbitrary requestId. The kept receipt's own `backupRef` is never read — the header carries the prior/kept/current diagram showing it rewinds one migration too far and discards schema the kept deploy applied.

REFUSES, NEVER SUBSTITUTES. Seven codes, each with FIXED prose in `ROLLBACK_RESTORE_DETAILS` keyed by code — no template, no interpolation, so no detail can be built out of a value just read: DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE, RESTORE_DEPLOY_UNKNOWN, RESTORE_MIGRATION_UNKNOWN, RESTORE_MIGRATION_UNVERIFIED (`readMigrationReceipt` THROWS on a corrupt record; caught, message discarded), RESTORE_BACKUP_ABSENT (null backupRef), RESTORE_BACKUP_UNVERIFIED (malformed ref, unreadable/empty artifact, or measured hash != recorded), RESTORE_FAILED. Every one leaves the database untouched. `splitBackupRef` splits on the LAST `@sha256:` so a path may contain anything, and validates the 64-hex tail.

ONE ATTEMPT (DoD 3): `ports.restoreDatabaseInto` is called exactly once, inside a try whose catch returns RESTORE_FAILED. No retry, no recovery pass.

ALSO AMENDED STEP 2's PORT, because step 3's "no partial apply" made the gap visible: added `--single-transaction` to the psql argv. Plain `pg_dump` output is NOT transaction-wrapped, so `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` alone would abort mid-restore and leave a half-applied schema. With it, "a restore that fails leaves the schema as it was" (DoD 3) is a property of the operation rather than a hope.

ROSTER HAZARD MEASURED AND AVOIDED (global rail 19 / mem:new-layer-constant-must-reuse-a-rostered-layer): `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:40-42) is CLOSED to four — DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED, DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT, DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING — enforced by `decodeRefusal` at :143-151 AND mirrored in `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts:84`, validated at :310. The refusals therefore leave at the SEAM as `DomainRefusal(code, DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM, detail)`, which is the discipline `rollback-command.ts` already uses for every other "the rollback could not proceed" path. `ROLLBACK_RESTORE_STAMP = "DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM"` is named `_STAMP`, not `_LAYER`, so `tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts` does not class it a new public boundary owing a roster row — the same reason `DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP` is named that way. implementationPlan.description: COMPOSE IT INTO THE COMMAND (DoD 1, 2), in `apps/daemon/src/deployment/rollback-command.ts`. Replace the UNCONDITIONAL refusal at :86-89 with the real path: when `request.restore` is true, resolve through step 3's binding and apply the dump to the bound destination via step 2's port; when the destination will not resolve, refuse `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` exactly as today, with the same code and layer, so the unbound case is unchanged for its existing asserters. WHEN `restore` IS NOT REQUESTED, NO RESTORE CALL IS MADE AT ALL — not a call with a null argument, not a no-op invocation: the port records nothing, because DoD 2 asserts both arms from the port's RECORDED CALLS. ORDERING: resolve and validate the restore BEFORE any irreversible rollback effect, so a restore that cannot proceed refuses without having half-rolled-back the deployment. THE ROLLBACK RECEIPT SAYS WHAT HAPPENED: a completed restore is recorded as applied; a failed restore records REFUSED with the failing step named, its code and its layer (DoD 3). CHANGE NOTHING ELSE in this file — replay identity, the intent record, the environment guard leg and receipt validation stay exactly as they are. The image-side rollback hardening is task-da60dc4b's, not this row's. Add the new port to the production composition so a REAL dispatch reaches it, not only an injected test object.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WHERE THE DESTINATION COMES FROM. Reusing `resolveDeployMigrationContext` versus writing a rollback-specific resolver: REUSE, decisively. The module was built to be shared with the revert, it already forwards `readEnvironmentDelivery`'s code AND layer unchanged, and it already confines the connection value. A second resolver is exactly the drift its header warns about, and a revert that restores a DIFFERENT database than the migration touched is the worst failure this row can ship. Rejected alternatives are named in that module's own comment and were re-measured: `process.env` is forbidden by DoD 1, a browser-supplied URL is forbidden by DoD 1 and epic rail 3, `launchDelivery` turns an unreadable store into "no database" and would restore nothing while reporting success.

WHERE THE RESTORE OPERATION LIVES. Extending `BackupPorts` with a destination-bound restore, versus a new port interface local to rollback. EXTEND `BackupPorts`: the dump side already takes a connection (`database(connection, destination)`), so the asymmetry is the defect, and `nodeBackupPorts` already owns the docker/psql argv, the `sanitized()` wrapper that strips messages into `BACKUP_FAILED`, and the container teardown discipline. A parallel interface would duplicate all four. The new operation is additive - `restoreDatabase(path)` keeps its verification meaning for `scheduled-backup.ts:62`, which must NOT change behaviour.

WHICH DUMP - see codebaseInsights (5). Put to the operator rather than guessed, because the two readings differ by exactly one migration and the literal DoD reading silently discards schema.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT TAKE. The image-side rollback hardening (previous image redeployed without rebuild) is task-da60dc4b's and is not touched here. This row changes the DATABASE arm only: the blanket refusal becomes conditional on whether a destination is bound, and everything else in `rollback-command.ts` - replay identity, the intent record, the environment guard leg, receipt validation - is left exactly as it is.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD BY architect-d6d49adc 2026-09-07.

(1) THE REFUSAL, CONFIRMED. `rollback-command.ts:86-89` refuses `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_DATABASE_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` for ANY `request.restore`, unconditionally, before the deploy receipt is even read. Its comment states the cause exactly: "BackupPorts.restoreDatabase verifies a dump in a temporary isolated database. It has no bound production restore destination."

(2) THE PORT GAP IS PRECISE. `BackupPorts` (backup-ports.ts:10-15) has `store(source,destination)`, `database(connection,destination)`, `restoreStore(path)`, `restoreDatabase(path)`. THE DUMP SIDE TAKES A CONNECTION; THE RESTORE SIDE DOES NOT. `restoreDatabase` (:116-131) runs `postgres:17-alpine` with `--rm -d --network none`, restores into THAT throwaway container, re-dumps and returns `BackupProof {sha256, restoredSha256}` - a verification, never a destination write. The row's job is a destination-bound restore beside it, mirroring `database(connection, destination)`'s shape.

(3) THE CREDENTIAL SEAM ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST BE REUSED, NOT REWRITTEN. `deploy-migration-context.ts` (159 lines, landed by task-2db55fca) exports `resolveDeployMigrationContext` and resolves the per-environment database value through `readEnvironmentDelivery` - explicitly NOT `process.env`, NOT `resolveEnvironmentLaunch` (its `PURPOSE_ENVIRONMENTS` is `{PREVIEW, VERIFIER}` with no deploy member) and NOT `launchDelivery` (coerces refusal to `undefined`). Its own header says it exists to be "RESOLVED ONCE AND REUSED BY THE REVERT", and warns that resolving a DIFFERENT database than the migration used is the worst outcome the slice can produce. It also mints refusals from a FIXED detail table keyed by code, so no call site can build a message out of the value it just read. That is DoD 1's "existing environment credential seam" and DoD 4's no-connection-value-in-evidence, already solved. A second resolver here would be the drift that header warns about.

(4) THE DEPLOY RECEIPT HAS NO backupRef. `RECEIPT_KEYS` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:82-85) is twelve: decidedAt, decisionId, environment, imageDigest, outcome, projectId, receiptId, refusal, releaseDecision, sha, url, version. `backupRef` lives ONLY on the MIGRATION receipt (migration-receipt.ts:22-36). They are joined durably: `deploy-command.ts:267` passes `requestId: decisionId`, so DEPLOY RECEIPT `decisionId` === MIGRATION RECEIPT `requestId`, resolvable by the deterministic `migrationReceiptId(projectId, requestId)` via `readMigrationReceipt`. A key lookup, never a filename/SHA/timestamp match.

(5) WHICH DUMP - SETTLED BY THE OPERATOR, 2026-09-07, because the two readings differ by one migration and the wrong one destroys data. `migrateWithBackup` dumps BEFORE it applies, so a receipt's `backupRef` is the schema as it was BEFORE that receipt's own migration. Rolling back from CURRENT to KEPT must restore THE CURRENT DEPLOY'S pre-migration dump - the state the kept receipt ran against. The literal DoD phrase "the one named by the kept deploy receipt" would restore the KEPT receipt's own backupRef, which predates the kept deploy's OWN migration and rewinds one step too far, discarding schema the kept deploy applied. DECIDED: current deploy's pre-migration dump. Absent current receipt, absent migration receipt or null backupRef REFUSES - it never falls back to another dump.

(6) THE LIVE-ARM PRECEDENT IS LANDED; DoD 4 needs no new harness. `migrate-down-real.test.ts` is the template: `const RUN = process.env.MOE_MIGRATION_RESTORE === "1"`, `it.runIf(RUN)(...)` for the live arm, `createVerifierDatabaseRunner` (orchestrator/verifier-database.ts) for the disposable-database lifecycle, nested `finally` teardown, and an assertion that Docker reports NO container left (epic rail 4). Crucially it ALSO carries an ALWAYS-RUNNING arm at :84 - "pins the live gate and the actual dispatch/engine imports" - so the file can never silently execute nothing. That arm is the discriminator global rail 8 demands and this row must copy it. NOTE: task-8f86e105 (WORKING, disposable PostgreSQL) is about the SCAFFOLD PROFILE's migration tooling - a different subject; this row does not wait on it.

(7) DEPENDENCIES BOTH DONE: task-95e68a8d (scheduled backups / BackupPorts) and task-b22462cf (deployment.rollback wired, human-fenced). Sibling task-da60dc4b (PLANNING) keeps the refusal code+layer assertion and the no-restore-call assertion - after this row those assertions belong to the UNBOUND-environment case, not to every restore. Coordination comment filed on that row.

Every refusal must fail CLOSED - an unresolvable destination, an absent current receipt, an absent migration receipt, a null backupRef, or a backup file that does not hash to what the receipt recorded must all REFUSE and leave the database untouched.
